---- Applicant Versus State Of Chhattisgarh Through- Police Station Nagarnarr District- Jagdalpur
Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent For Applicant : Mr. Priyank Rathi, Advocate For State : Mr. Pramod Shrivastava,
Dy. Govt. Advocate S.B.: Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge Order On Board 16/04/2024
1.

These two bail applications filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail are being disposed off by this common order as both the applications arise out of same crime number.
2.
Applicants are arrested in connection with Crime No.236 of 2023 registered at Police Station - Nagarnar, Jagdalpur, Bastar (CG), for offence punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471, 409, 34 of IPC.

3. Case of the prosecution, in brief is that, report has been lodged in concerned police station stating that on 05.12.2023 in connivance with the Supervisor of the Nagarnaar Plant, in truck bearing No.CG04-MK-9383, CG04-M-6058, pig iron was loaded more than the capacity mentioned in the slip and thereby the management of plant was defrauded to the tune of Rs.6,20,926/-.
Based on the said report, instant crime was registered and during investigation, memorandum statement of co-accused Ajij Ahmed and statement of one Karim Ahmed under Section 161 CrPC was recorded.
Applicants have been arrayed as accused and they were arrested.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant- Jagatram Nag submits that applicant has been made accused only on the basis of memorandum statement of co-accused.
He is alleged to have been working as Supervisor in NMDC which is absolutely baseless.
Applicant was appointed as Labour and he used to do the work of muck cleaning.

Other co-accused person Arvind Kumar Paul in whose memorandum statement name of applicant has come that he is also involved in commission of crime and is Supervisor, has been enlarged on bail vide order dated 28.03.2024 passed in MCRC No. 2136 of 2024 .
Applicant being Labour is not aware as to who had loaded extra quantity of pig iron in the truck driven by Arbaz Khan and Aziz Ahmed.

Applicant is in jail since 13.12.2023,
investigation is complete, charge sheet has been filed, hence, he may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned counsel for applicant- Brijesh Alam submits that applicant is also a Labour and was found present at the time of incident.
There is no material in the entire charge sheet to show that applicant was deputed by NMDC as Supervisor.
Applicant was implicated only on the basis of memorandum statement of Trilochan Bhatagoi.
There is no other criminal antecedents of the applicant.
He is in jail since 12.12.2023, after completion of investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Two other similarly situated accused persons have been enlarged on bail, hence, the applicant may also be released on regular bail.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposed the submission of learned counsel for the applicants.
They submit that applicants are involved in commission of offence.

Both the applicants are working as Supervisor and at their instance excess quantity of pig iron was loaded in the truck which has come in the memorandum statement of co-accused Arvind Kumar Paul and Trilochan Bhatagoi.
However, upon asking with regard to letter/any document showing appointment of the applicants to be Supervisor, they submit that in the case diary/charge sheet there is no such document available.
Upon further asking, they submits that there is no criminal antecedents of the applicants.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

8. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, submission of learned counsel for the respective parties and further considering that two other similarly situated accused persons have been enlarged on bail in MCRC No.1949 of 2024 and MCRC No.2136 of 2024, after completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed and that there is no criminal antecedents of the applicants, without commenting anything on merit of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicants on bail.
9.
Accordingly, the bail applications are allowed.

It is directed that the applicants shall be released on regular bail on each of them furnishing a personal bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that:-.
a) Applicants shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) Applicants shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
